I've found the bug. Let me confirm the diagnosis by comparing the input and output.

**The bug:** In the minified output, several label *definitions* are silently deleted even though they're still referenced. Compare:
- Input line 120 `waitForHot:` → **gone** from output (output jumps from `j r12` line 77 straight to `l r0 habSensor Temperature` line 78)
- Same for `waitForPressure:`, `pressureDone:`, `waitForCold:`, `waitForVacuum:`, `vacuumDone:`

Yet line 14 of the output still says `move r12 waitForHot` — referencing a label that no longer exists. The output is broken.

**Root cause:** [extension.js:47-60](extension.js#L47-L60) `collectLabelRefs` only treats a label as "used" when it appears as the **last operand of a branch instruction** (`j`, `beq`, etc.). But in IC10 a label name is just a line-number constant and can be used as an operand in *any* instruction. Your code uses them in `move`:

```
move coolingState waitForHot        # waitForHot referenced via move, not a branch
```

Since `move` isn't in `branchOps`, `waitForHot` (and the other six state labels) are never added to `labelRefs`, so [extension.js:84](extension.js#L84) strips their definitions as "unused" — while the `move` lines that reference them survive. The labels referenced by branches (`tickStart`, `craft`, `clear`, `eject`, `releaseCold`) are kept, which is why only *some* labels disappear.

The same flaw exists in [convertLabelsToLineNumbers](extension.js#L156-L193) (ABSOLUTE), which only rewrites labels in branch ops, so `move r12 waitForHot` would never get its line number.

Let me fix both functions so a label is recognized as any operand token matching a known label name.

Confirmed correct. Line index 73 is `l r0 habSensor Temperature` — exactly the instruction that followed `waitForHot:`. No label definitions or unresolved label references remain.

## Summary

**The bug:** Labels referenced only through non-branch instructions were being treated as unused and deleted.

Your script uses labels as line-number values in `move` instructions:
```
move coolingState waitForHot
```
This is valid IC10 — a label is just a line-number constant and can be an operand of *any* instruction. But the minifier's `collectLabelRefs` only scanned the **last operand of branch ops** (`j`, `beq`, …). So `waitForHot`, `waitForPressure`, `pressureDone`, `waitForCold`, `waitForVacuum`, and `vacuumDone` — referenced only via `move` — were never marked as used, and [extension.js:84](extension.js#L84) stripped their definitions while leaving the `move` lines pointing at deleted labels. Broken output.

**The fix** (two functions, same root cause):
- [collectLabelRefs](extension.js#L47-L65): now marks *any* operand token matching a known label name as a reference, regardless of opcode.
- [convertLabelsToLineNumbers](extension.js#L155-L186): now rewrites label operands in *any* instruction (not just branch ops), so `move r12 waitForHot` → `move r12 73` in ABSOLUTE mode.

Both skip the leading label-definition token and the opcode, and ignore quoted strings/comments as before.

**Verified:** all 11 labels are now retained through minify, and ABSOLUTE conversion resolves every label (including the `move` references) to the correct line number with no dangling references.

One note: the stale outputs in `Testing/` (e.g. `Labels in Non-Branch Instructions Bug MINIFIED.ic10`) were generated by the old buggy code. Re-run the command to regenerate them. Want me to bump the version in `package.json` / changelog for this fix?

function collectLabelRefs(lines,labelSet){
  // A label name is a line-number constant in IC10 and can appear as an operand of
  // ANY instruction (e.g. `move coolingState waitForHot`), not just branch ops.
  // Treat every operand token that matches a known label name as a reference.
  const refs=new Set();
  for(let idx=0; idx<lines.length; idx++){
    const raw=lines[idx]; const parts=splitQuotedSegments(raw);
    let code=parts.filter(p=>!p.quoted).map(p=>p.text).join(' ');
    code=code.replace(/#.*$/,'');
    const tokens=code.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean); if(tokens.length===0) continue;
    // Skip a leading label-definition token (e.g. "loop:") and the opcode itself.
    let start=0;
    if(/^[A-Za-z_][\w$]*:$/.test(tokens[0])) start=1;
    for(let t=start+1; t<tokens.length; t++){
      const tok=tokens[t];
      if(/^[A-Za-z_][\w$]*$/.test(tok) && labelSet.has(tok)) refs.add(tok);
    }
  }
  return refs;

Found it. This is the real cause:

```
florpydorp.ic10-safe-minifier@1.0.8   ← installed in your normal VS Code
```

You have an **old copy (v1.0.8) installed** as a regular extension. Your edits are confirmed present in `c:\Dev\Minifier Repo\extension.js` (the fix string is there, file saved at 19:30) — that's the file F5 loads. So the dev code is fine. The problem is *which* copy actually handles the command.

**Why F5 "used to" work and now doesn't:** The Extension Development Host only overrides the installed copy of the same extension ID *inside that separate `[Extension Development Host]` window*. When you press F5, a new window opens running your edited code — but if you run minify in your **main** window (or look at output generated there), you get the installed **v1.0.8**, which is old, pre-fix code. In your earlier sessions you didn't have a stale installed copy sitting there intercepting, so whatever window you used ran the dev code. Now v1.0.8 shadows you whenever you're not strictly in the dev-host window.

(Note: there's also `florpydorp.florpydorp-ic10-language-support@2.2.0` installed — that's a *different* extension, just syntax highlighting, not the minifier. Not the culprit.)

Two ways to fix it cleanly:

**Option A — keep using the F5 dev-host flow (your old habit).** Just make sure you run the command in the window whose title says **`[Extension Development Host]`**. To remove all ambiguity, uninstall the stale installed copy so nothing can shadow:
```
code --uninstall-extension florpydorp.ic10-safe-minifier
```
Then F5, open the `.ic10` in the new window, Ctrl+Alt+Y there.

**Option B — just update the installed copy** so your normal window runs new code:
```
# bump package.json to 1.1.1, then:
vsce package
code --install-extension ic10-safe-minifier-1.1.1.vsix --force
# reload window
```

I'd go with **Option A** since that matches how you like to work, and the uninstall removes the exact thing that's confusing you. Want me to run the uninstall command for you? (You'd then press F5 yourself.) Or if you prefer Option B, I'll bump + package + install.
